reader_question: How are the House’s seats divided by party today?
grade_line: Documented: the House Clerk’s count of its members
title: Republicans held 218 of the House’s 435 seats on November 11, 2026, and Democrats 214, with one independent and two seats vacant.
measure_line: Voting seats in the U.S. House of Representatives by the party of the member who holds each, as the Clerk of the House counted them on November 11, 2026
notes: At the opening of the 119th Congress in January 2025, Republicans held 220 seats and Democrats 215; deaths, resignations and special elections since then changed the count.
A majority of the full House is 218 seats. Members elected on November 3, 2026 take their seats on January 3, 2027.
source_line: Source: Office of the Clerk, U.S. House of Representatives, party breakdown, as of November 11, 2026; U.S. House of Representatives, Office of the Historian and Office of the Clerk (History, Art & Archives), Party Divisions of the House of Representatives, 119th Congress (2025 to 2027). Retrieved November 11, 2026. The count changes with each vacancy and special election.
alt: A half circle of 435 dots, one for each House seat: 214 Democrats from the left, then one independent and two empty seats, then 218 Republicans to the right. A tick marks the 218th seat from the right, a majority of the full House.

table.caption: House seats by party, as of November 11, 2026

columns.label: Party, as the Clerk lists it

chart_notes: Every seat is drawn in one ink, so no color stands for a party; each block is named with its count. The two empty seats are open rings.

majority.label: 218, a majority of the full House
